events.label: Sabaeans

source.title: Slavery in First Millennium Arabia: Epigraphy and the Qurʾān
source.author: Valentina A. Grasso

events.update: Post-2015 epigraphic synthesis directly engages pre-Islamic South Arabian inscriptions. It cautions that ʿbd can be ambiguous, while evidence of captives and people bought/sold as personal property establishes enslavement in first-millennium South Arabia. For the atlas row this is sufficient to move from generic regional plausibility to a bounded Sabaean/South-Arabian support state, without any prevalence claim.

events.label: Chámpa
events.update: Later synthesis independently places Chams within medieval East-Asian captivity/enslavement histories and stresses the unevenness of early evidence. It corroborates the slavery/captivity context but does not expand the 1300 territorial-prevalence claim.

events.label: Alodia
events.update: Bounded 2016–2026 search did not produce a credible genuinely new target-specific source sufficient to alter the frozen 2015 state.

events.label: Janapada of Aśmaka
events.update: No credible genuinely new Aśmaka-specific 2016–2026 slavery/dependency source was accepted within the bounded search.

events.label: Cao

source.title: Slavery and Forced Labour in Early China and the Roman World
source.author: Walter Scheidel

events.update: Later comparative scholarship strengthens the broader early-China slavery/forced-labour context but remains non-Cao-specific and does not overcome the target-level abstention.
